title: Amanda: Unified Instrumentation Framework for Deep Neural Networks
problem: Current DNN analysis and optimization tasks (tracing, pruning, quantization) have ad-hoc implementations in TensorFlow/PyTorch backends, requiring developers to manage fragmented interfaces and repeatedly adapt code across different models and backends.
motivation: Unified instrumentation frameworks reduce development burden and enable writing analysis/optimization tools once that work across multiple DNN backends and execution modes.
method: Amanda provides two layers of tools for analyzing and optimizing neural networks. The user-facing layer lets developers easily add measurement points (instrumentation) at each operation level—the individual steps that make up neural networks—while the internal layer uses callbacks (functions triggered by events) to efficiently run both the original code and the measurement-enhanced version. This design works with deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch, supporting both graph mode (code compiled before running) and eager mode (code runs line-by-line as written).
key_novelty: Amanda unifies neural network analysis and optimization through operation-level measurement (instrumentation), using a two-layer tool design that balances ease-of-use with efficiency across deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch.
contributions: Unified instrumentation framework abstracting diverse DNN analysis/optimization tasks as operator-level instrumentation
Dual-level API design enabling backend-agnostic instrumentation with efficient execution management
Support across multiple backends (TensorFlow/PyTorch) and execution modes (graph/eager)
Practical implementation demonstrating <5% performance overhead for tracing, profiling, pruning, and quantization
